description: Search receipt-linked US government financial disclosures. Both chambers of Congress under the STOCK Act, plus executive-branch OGE filings -- filter chamber='executive' for those, which is where the President's disclosures are. Every row resolves to the government's own PDF via receipt.url — cite it. Supports point-in-time reconstruction via as_of (rows observed on or before that timestamp; no look-ahead bias) and change polling via updated_since. Paginate with the returned page.next_cursor.

as_of.description: ISO timestamp: only rows first observed on/before this instant

chamber.description: Filter by filing body. 'house' and 'senate' are STOCK Act periodic transaction reports; 'executive' is executive-branch OGE filings, which is where the President's disclosures are. Omit to search all.

cursor.description: Opaque page.next_cursor from a previous call

limit.description: Rows per page (free tier caps at 25; licensed 1000)

member_id.description: Filter to one filer by slug, e.g. donald-trump or nancy-pelosi. Use list_members to resolve a name to its identifier.

min_delay_days.description: Only rows filed at least this many days after the transaction. The STOCK Act window is 45 days, so 46 returns filings outside it. Rows without a computed delay are excluded, not guessed at.

ticker.description: Filter by ticker symbol, e.g. NVDA

updated_since.description: ISO timestamp: only rows first observed after this instant

within_statutory_window.description: false returns only filings made outside the statutory window that applies to that row (served as statutory_window_days); true returns only filings inside it. Prefer this over min_delay_days when the question is 'was it late', because the boundary is the row's own window, not a number you supply. Annual reports have no window and are excluded by either value.

name: search_disclosures

out_of_range.description: True when requested_as_of predates retained point-in-time history. This is distinct from a genuine empty result.

point_in_time_floor.description: Inclusive lower bound for as_of and updated_since. Requests one millisecond before this instant are refused rather than returned as an empty result.

rows_dropped_failed_validation.description: Rows withheld because the serving view and executable response contract disagreed. Any value above zero means the page is partial.

amount.description: The bounded range exactly as disclosed. A missing amount is never estimated.

basis.description: States what the amount fields are: the bounded range as the filing disclosed it. The only basis served today; a future exact-amount source would carry its own.

currency.description: Always USD. Every disclosure form Veridion serves reports in dollars.

midpoint.description: Veridion's arithmetic midpoint of range_low and range_high, rounded to the dollar. It is a convenience, not a disclosed value: the filer reported a band, never a figure. Absent when the band is open-ended ("over", "more than", "less than" and their variants) because a midpoint of an unbounded range is invented. Use it only with the range shown beside it.

range_high.description: Upper bound of the disclosed band, in whole USD. For an open-ended band such as "over $50,000,000" this is the stated threshold, and midpoint is absent.

range_low.description: Lower bound of the band the filing discloses, in whole USD, as printed on the form ($1,001 to $15,000 serves 1001).

verbatim_text.description: The amount text exactly as it appears on the filing, before any parsing. When range_low and range_high disagree with this text, this text is the filing.

asset.description: The instrument as the filing names it, classified from the office's own asset code. Nothing is resolved against a securities master; a ticker is served only when the filing states one.

asset_type.description: Classified from the office's own asset code on congressional filings: ST equity, OP option, MF and EF fund, GS government_security, PS partnership, CT crypto, anything else other. OGE lines carry equity, fund or other. etf, municipal_bond and corporate_bond are reserved in the enum and produced by no current source.

description.description: Free-text description from the filing's asset line when the office publishes one separately from the name; null otherwise. Never composed by Veridion.

name.description: The asset as named on the filing, whitespace collapsed. If the filing names nothing but gives a ticker, the ticker; if it gives neither, the literal "Disclosed asset" so the row is not silently dropped.

source_code.description: The asset code exactly as the office recorded it (ST, OP, MF, EF, GS, PS, CT and others), upper-cased; the input to asset_type. Null when the source carries none.

ticker.description: The ticker as it appears on the filing, upper-cased; null when the filing states none (most OGE lines, bonds, funds without a symbol, and paper filings whose ticker column is blank). Not looked up or inferred from the asset name.

change.description: Full pulls contain upserts. updated_since also emits supersede events; remove the row only when version_id matches the version held locally. A withdrawn stable identifier remains directly retrievable with its reason.

observed_at.description: When Veridion observed the event this row reports (the version's first observation for an upsert; the supersession instant for a supersede).

reason.description: Why a row was withdrawn or superseded, when the pipeline recorded one; null for an ordinary upsert. States the mechanism, never a motive.

state.description: active: served in snapshot reads. withdrawn: no longer served in snapshots but still directly retrievable by disclosure_id, with reason set.

type.description: upsert: this version is the one to hold. supersede: a version you may hold has been replaced, and is only emitted on updated_since reads.

content_hash.description: sha256, hex, of the canonical JSON array ["veridion-disclosure-content-v1", disclosure_id, version_id, member.member_id, member.full_name, member.chamber, asset.ticker, asset.name, asset.asset_type, asset.source_code, asset.description, transaction.type, transaction.date, filing.type, filing.filed_date, amount.range_low, amount.range_high, amount.verbatim_text, owner.label, owner.determination, receipt.document_id, receipt.url, receipt.source_system, receipt.page, provenance.source_line_number] using the served values exactly (null where null). Recompute it from this row to check the calculation; store it to check later that the same version_id still serves the same content. Derived fields (delay_days, statutory window, midpoint), timestamps, parser and methodology versions, and the change block are excluded, so a corrected derivation rule does not change the hash of an unchanged filing. The basis label changes if the field list ever changes.

disclosure_id.description: Permanent identifier for the filing-derived transaction. It is never reused; parser versions and restatements retain this identifier.

filing.description: The report this row was parsed from and its timing against the STOCK Act's 45-day transaction window, computed from the two dates on the filing.

delay_days.description: filed_date minus transaction.date, in whole days, as the two dates appear on the filing. Null when either is absent. Not clamped: a filing that predates its own transaction would serve a negative value rather than a corrected one.

filed_date.description: The date the office records the report as filed. The STOCK Act window and delay_days are measured to this date.

statutory_window_days.description: 45 for a periodic transaction report, the STOCK Act's transaction-level reporting window; null for annual reports and unknown forms, which carry no per-transaction deadline. A constant of the form, not a per-row judgement. Note that 45 days from the transaction is only one of the two clocks: a report is due by the EARLIER of 45 days from the transaction or 30 days from the filer being notified of it. The House PTR form includes a notification-date column; this dataset does not capture it, so the 30-day clock is not represented here.

type.description: periodic_transaction_report for House Clerk and Senate eFD PTRs and OGE Form 278-T; annual_report for OGE Form 278e; null when the receipt URL matches no known form pattern. Determined from the office and receipt, not from the row's text.

within_statutory_window.description: Present only when the filing type has an applicable transaction-level window and delay_days is known. True means delay_days <= statutory_window_days -- that is, within the 45-day transaction clock. It does NOT mean the filing was timely: the 30-day notification clock may have expired first, and we do not measure it. Do not treat this field as a compliance determination.

identity_basis.description: Identity uses only filer, document, filed instrument, transaction date and type, amount range, and owner. Parser line, span, version, and run identifiers are excluded.

member.description: The filer, resolved against the congressional directory where a match exists. Identity fields only; what the filing itself says is in the receipt.

chamber.description: house or senate from the office that published the receipt; executive for Office of Government Ethics filers.

district.description: House district as `STATE-N` with N an integer and 0 an at-large seat (`GA-14`, `AK-0`); null for senators, executive-branch filers, and rows whose filing does not state one. The same form the /v1/members directory uses.

full_name.description: The filer's name from the official directory where matched; otherwise the name as it appears on the filing with honorifics (Hon., Sen., Rep.) removed.

member_id.description: Veridion's stable identifier for the filer, the same value /v1/members/{member_id} resolves and the member_id= filter takes. Derived from the name as filed; it does not change across filings or restatements.

party.description: Democrat, Republican or Independent, from the congressional directory's D, R or I; null when the directory records none and for every executive-branch filer.

person_id.description: The filer's official Bioguide ID (for example G000596) where the congressional directory has one; null for executive-branch filers and for congressional filers the directory could not match. Never invented.

state.description: Two-letter state of the seat, as recorded in the congressional directory; null for executive-branch filers.

owner.description: Whose holding the transaction concerns, from the filing's Owner column, and how that value was established.

determination.description: How the owner value was established. owner_column_undetermined means the filing row was located but the extracted text did not positively establish whether its Owner column was blank.

label.description: The filing's Owner column: self, spouse, joint or dependent_child as marked; not_specified_in_filing when the official receipt was checked and the column is blank; undetermined when the row was located but the column could not be read with confidence. See determination for how the value was established.

provenance.description: How and when this version of the row was produced, and when the row was first observed, which is the instant as_of reads against. None of these fields is in content_hash.

first_observed_at.description: When Veridion first observed this row. Immutable and used by the as_of filter.

methodology_version.description: The admission and derivation rules this row was served under, currently receipt-or-drop-v1. A rule change ships as a new label and a changelog entry; see the stability policy.

parsed_at.description: When the parser generation named in parser_version produced this version of the row. A reparse under a new parser writes a new version with its own parsed_at; the earlier version stays in /history.

parser_version.description: The parser generation that produced this version (for example house-ptr-line-v2). Not part of content_hash, so a reparse that changes no filing fact changes no hash.

source_ingested_at.description: When the source record entered Veridion's warehouse. first_observed_at is never later than this; the two differ when identity resolution carried an earlier observation forward.

source_line_number.description: House Clerk PTR rows carry a PDF source-line coordinate when the parser recorded one; null rows are reconciled by reason, and parser-output gaps are enumerated in house_clerk_gap_register. Senate eFD records are parsed as filing transactions rather than House PTR PDF lines, so source_line_number is null by design.

transcription_method.description: Present only for OGE rows. pdf_text_layer means the official PDF text was parsed; verified_transcription means the row was read from a checked transcription whose SHA-256 matched the official scanned PDF at ingestion.

receipt.description: The government receipt this row was parsed from. Preserve the access label.

access.description: `gated` means the official Senate eFD URL requires acknowledging its access agreement before the filing is displayed; other supported sources are `open`.

content_type.description: MIME type of the document at receipt.url: application/pdf for House Clerk and OGE documents, text/html for Senate eFD filings, which the Senate publishes as pages.

document_id.description: The office's own identifier for the document: the House Clerk's numeric document id, the Senate eFD report id, or the OGE document id. Resolves at /v1/receipts/{document_id}.

page.description: Page of the document the row was parsed from, where the source is paginated and the parser recorded it (OGE filings); null for congressional rows, whose position is given by provenance.source_line_number instead.

retrieved_at.description: When Veridion's warehouse first recorded the source document this row comes from. Independent of provenance.parsed_at, which belongs to the parser generation and may be earlier when a later retrieval re-attached an existing parse.

source_system.description: The office that published the receipt: house_clerk, senate_efd or oge. sec_edgar is declared in the enum and serves no rows; /v1/status reports it as no_data.

url.description: The government's URL for the document this row was parsed from, on the office's own domain. Never a Veridion-hosted copy. Cite it beside any claim built on the row.

transaction.description: What was done and on what date, as stated on the filing.

date.description: The transaction date as stated on the filing. Not the filing date, and not adjusted for weekends or holidays.

type.description: buy from a P code or a purchase/buy label; sell from an S code or a sale/sell label; exchange from an E code or an exchange label; other for anything the filing marks differently. Partial versus full sale is not distinguished here; the filing's own wording is in amount.verbatim_text and the receipt.

version_id.description: Immutable parse-generation identifier. Use disclosure_id, not version_id, for downstream identity across a restatement.

next_cursor.description: Token generated from the last fetched row's position, before response validation, when another page exists and that position is valid; null otherwise. A disclosure cursor is a position token, not a credential. It carries the read mode, a fingerprint of the normalized filters, time boundaries, the pinned snapshot generation and pagination position; it carries no API key, license, tier, scope or authorization grant. Every replay authenticates the current caller independently and applies that caller's permissions, row cap and rate budget, including the free tier's limits. API-key rotation or revocation does not invalidate the cursor for another permitted caller; a revoked key itself is still refused. Later dataset generations do not advance the pinned generation. Replay still requires matching filters, retained snapshot history and the server's cursor-signing key; changing that signing key is distinct from rotating a client's API key and invalidates existing tokens. The current format contains no expiry field, which is not a guarantee of indefinite availability. The payload is readable base64url JSON protected by an HMAC, not encryption: time boundaries and position are visible, and ordinary filters are an unkeyed SHA256 fingerprint against which guesses can be tested offline. Treat a cursor as you would a URL containing your query: do not publish it or put it in shared logs, and return it unchanged rather than depending on its internal encoding.

next_updated_since.description: The watermark to pass as `updated_since` on the next incremental call, after walking this result set to its last page. It equals this response's pinned snapshot_as_of, so a caller that stores it receives everything changed after this response and nothing twice. It is always at or after the retained-history floor, so it is always a value this API accepts. Do NOT derive a watermark from a row's change.observed_at: rows observed before retained history began are served with their true observation instant, and that instant predates the floor. Added at 1.3.23 after a measured 98.7% of served rows carried such an instant.

requested_updated_since.description: The normalized updated_since filter applied to this incremental page. Null for a full snapshot pull.

snapshot_as_of.description: Pinned on page one and carried inside every cursor. Later writes cannot shift the result set during pagination.

snapshot_generation.description: Atomic dataset generation pinned on page one. A value of zero means the requested as_of predates retained exact payload history, or the current-row fallback is active while temporal history is unavailable.
